title: Parameter cut of a generating tuple at the expected codimension
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of dimension $d\ge1$, and let $t_1,\ldots,t_d\in\mathfrak m$ generate $\mathfrak m$. Let $1\le b\le d$, choose $z_2,\ldots,z_b\in\mathfrak m$, and set $I=(t_1,z_2,\ldots,z_b)$. Assume $\dim(R/I)=d-b$. Put $R'=R/(t_1)$, let $q:R\to R'$ be the quotient map, and put $I'=q(I)R'$. Then $R'$ is regular local of dimension $d-1$, its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m/(t_1)$, and $q(z_2),\ldots,q(z_b)$ is an $R'$-regular sequence in that maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] generating $I'$. The canonical quotient isomorphism $R'/I'\simeq R/I$ satisfies $\dim(R'/I')=(d-1)-(b-1)$. For every surjective local homomorphism $f:R\twoheadrightarrow S$ to a commutative local ring $S$ with $t_1\in\ker f$, the induced $f':R'\twoheadrightarrow S$ is local and $\dim R'-\dim S=(\dim R-\dim S)-1$. Here local means that maximal ideals map into maximal ideals, and $S$ has finite Krull dimension since it is a quotient of $R$. When $b=1$, the displayed regular sequence is empty, $I'=0$, and $R'/I'=R'$.

source.place: Tag 00SE (lemma-ci-well-defined), final paragraph: replace A by A/xA and I by I/xA, decreasing the dimension and generator count by one; fixed-tuple regularity is the dimension computation implicit in that reduction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] to the given ordered $d$-tuple, with prefix length $c=1$. Its hypotheses are exactly that $R$ is regular local of dimension $d$ and the tuple generates $\mathfrak m$. It gives that $R\prime=R/(t_1)$ is regular local of dimension $d-1$. Since $(t_1)\subseteq\mathfrak m$, [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure] identifies its maximal ideal as $\mathfrak m\prime=q(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak m/(t_1)$. In particular all $q(z_i)$ lie in $\mathfrak m\prime$.

source.place: Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), prefix c=1; Tags 00E9 (lemma-characterize-local-ring) and 07BJ (lemma-characterize-local-ring-map), quotient-local interpretation

proof.text: As $q(t_1)=0$, applying $q$ to the displayed generating expression for $I$ gives $I\prime=(q(z_2),\ldots,q(z_b))$. Define $\alpha:R\prime/I\prime\to R/I$ by $[q(r)]\mapsto[r]$, and its inverse by $[r]\mapsto[q(r)]$. Both are well-defined because $(t_1)\subseteq I$ and $q(I)$ vanishes modulo $I\prime$; the two composites fix every residue class. Pullback of prime ideals along these inverse ring maps identifies strict prime chains, hence their Krull dimensions agree [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Thus $\dim(R\prime/I\prime)=d-b=(d-1)-(b-1)$, using $1\le b\le d$. For $b=1$, the generator list is empty and $I\prime=0$.

source.place: Tag 00SE (lemma-ci-well-defined), final paragraph, quotient identification and dimension bookkeeping in A/xA and I/xA

proof.text: The ring $R\prime$ is nonzero because it is local. Its empty sequence is regular: the injectivity conditions are vacuous and the final quotient is $R\prime\ne0$, by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Apply [lem-trf-regular-local-regular-sequence-depth] to the regular local ring $R\prime$, with $c=0$ and this empty sequence. Its assertion for $i=0$ gives that $R\prime$ is Noetherian local and $\operatorname{depth}(R\prime)=\dim R\prime=d-1$.

source.place: Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), final sentence; Tag 02JN (lemma-reformulate-CM), empty-prefix instance

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-cm-regular-sequence-generator-count] with the Noetherian local ring $R\prime$, its finite dimension $d-1$, and the ordered $(b-1)$-tuple $(q(z_2),\ldots,q(z_b))$. Step 1 puts every entry in its maximal ideal, Step 3 supplies the depth hypothesis, and Step 2 supplies precisely the required quotient dimension. The criterion proves regularity of this very tuple, which generates $I\prime$ by Step 2. It includes $b=1$: the sequence is empty and $R\prime/I\prime=R\prime$.

source.place: Tag 02JN (lemma-reformulate-CM), displayed equivalence, applied after the parameter cut in Tag 00SE (lemma-ci-well-defined)

proof.text: For the given $f$, define $f\prime(q(r))=f(r)$. If $q(r)=q(s)$ then $r-s\in(t_1)\subseteq\ker f$, proving well-definedness; its ring laws and surjectivity follow directly from those of $f$. Every member of $\mathfrak m\prime$ is $q(a)$ for $a\in\mathfrak m$, so $f\prime(\mathfrak m\prime)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$ by locality of $f$. To check finiteness of $\dim S$, pull a strict prime chain of $S$ back along $f$: preimages are prime because $S/P$ is a domain, and remain strict because a witness in a difference has a lift under the surjection. Chain lengths are therefore at most $d$, while $S$ has its maximal prime ideal; by [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], $0\le\dim S\le d$. Using Step 1, integer arithmetic now gives $\dim R\prime-\dim S=(d-1)-\dim S=(\dim R-\dim S)-1$.
